name: Teshenawa
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. 2001. Shira, Teshena, Auyo: Hausa's (former) eastern neighbors. In Derek Nurse (ed.), Historical Language Contact in Africa (= Sprache und Geschichte in Afrika 16/17), 387-435. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. §3.1-3.2 (pp. 399-402): the entire Teshena corpus is two word lists (Teshena I, 1921; Teshena II, 1926/27) in an unpublished report by colonial officer P. G. Harris (1927, Kaduna Archives) from the last two rememberers; p. 402: 'They did not mark tone or vowel length.' Phonological discussion is limited to segmental sound changes (voicing dissimilation, resyllabification) and morphology.

sources.citation: Bross, Michael. 1997. Some remarks on the history of extinct languages Auyo, Shira and Teshena. In Seidensticker, Bross & Baba (eds.), Guddiri studies: languages and rock paintings in northeastern Nigeria (Westafrikanische Studien), 37-65. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Only other linguistic treatment of Teshena; would confirm that nothing beyond the Harris lists exists. Very unlikely to contain a stress statement (same unmarked source data).

sources.citation: Harris, P. Graham. 1927. Report of the District Officer, Katagum Division, to the Resident, Bauchi Province, 1 Feb 1927, with appended Teshena vocabularies (Teshena I 1921, Teshena II 1926/27). Kaduna: National Archives (unpublished).

sources.note: The sole primary record of the language; Schuh reports it marks no tone/length, but the ~75 sentences of Teshena II were only partly reproduced by Schuh. For completeness only; no prosodic marking expected.

sources.citation: Broß, Michael. 1996. On the classification of extinct languages: The case of Shiranci and Teshenanci. Berichte des Sonderforschungsbereichs 268, 8: 35-36.
